solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: List of terms has boy admitting defeat

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so the boy's name takes the other word inside it

parts.note: Gary is a boy's name
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: A lad owns up to being beaten, and somehow a list of terms is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is the alphabetical word list with meanings at the back of a book, a list of terms.

clue.text: Decorate bottom of gown with ostentatious surrounding?

indicators.note: placed around, so the showy word encloses the letter from the gown

parts.note: garish means loud and showy

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Trimming the hem of a gown with something flashy all round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To garnish is to adorn or embellish, usually food, a synonym for decorate.

clue.text: Brain, perhaps: it's stopped

definitions.meaning: the brain is an example of a body part with its own function
a pipe instrument fitted with stops that select its voices

explanation.surface: Is the brain, say, one that has stopped working?
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's stopped' seems to mean ceased, but it refers to an instrument equipped with stops.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is a bodily organ; the church instrument with pipes and stops shares the name.

clue.text: Placed bottom, is mill passable?

parts.note: to put one's bottom down is to sit, so sat
a mill is a factory

explanation.surface: Someone sat down asks whether the mill is up to standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable and satisfactory both mean adequate, good enough without being excellent.

clue.text: Illegally take in bird

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: An instruction to poach a bird by unlawful means.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a familiar small songbird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Leg in which the favourites turned over

indicators.note: something turned over is upended, so the word for the favourites is read backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: A race leg in which the favourites fell or were overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg of a journey or contest is one stage of it, a synonym for a single stage.

clue.text: I have not finished in test that's unimportant

indicators.note: placed inside, so the shortened phrase goes into the test

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: lacking its end, so the final letter of the contraction goes

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone admits they never completed a test that did not matter much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have' is read as the contraction I'VE, and 'not finished' drops its final E; 'in' places the remainder inside the test word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means slight or of little consequence, a synonym for unimportant.

clue.text: Eternal youth, taking to children's entertainment

parts.note: Peter Pan is the boy who never grows up

explanation.surface: The secret of eternal youth applied to entertaining children.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is pantomime, the British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a festive theatre show aimed largely at children.

clue.text: Moving along, earner becoming rich capitalist?

indicators.note: letters on the move are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the clue prints the singular earner, but the answer needs a plural's S here; the setter appears to have dropped it

explanation.surface: A wage earner moving on up to become a wealthy capitalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter slipped: 'Moving' rearranges along and earner, which lack the S the answer needs. 'capitalist' means a resident of the capital, London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sloane Ranger is a wealthy, upper-class young Londoner, named after Sloane Square; capitalist here means someone of the capital.

clue.text: OK to be Conservatives

definitions.meaning: the political wing of conservatives is called by the opposite of left

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is acceptable to be a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct or acceptable is one sense; in politics the conservative side is known by the same word.

clue.text: Bengali disguised as European

indicators.note: a disguised thing has its appearance changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from Bengal passes himself off as someone from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Belgium is a native of a European country, so an example of a European.

clue.text: Not opening, European pub

indicators.note: without its opening letter, so the first letter of the European goes

parts.note: a Finn is a European, from Finland

explanation.surface: A European pub that is not open for business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not opening' reads as a closed pub, but it removes the first letter of FINN.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a traditional pub or tavern offering drink and often lodging.

clue.text: Small state where Romanians dispersed

indicators.note: scattered in all directions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny country where a group of Romanians went their separate ways.
explanation.definitionFit: This microstate enclaved within Italy is one of the smallest independent countries in Europe.

clue.text: Who had ordered seat on jumbo?

indicators.note: put in order, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A question about who requested a seat on a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbo' suggests an aircraft, but here it is an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is a canopied seat carried on an elephant's back; jumbo is a nickname for an elephant.

clue.text: Royal house turns on old king

parts.note: winds means twists or turns
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A royal household changes allegiance and turns against an elderly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Windsor is the British royal family's dynasty name since 1917.

clue.text: Cry with pained expression, being cowardly

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
ow is the expression of someone in pain

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks and grimaces, showing themselves a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is an informal word for lacking courage, as in yellow-bellied.

clue.text: Pay to keep soldier in Oxfordshire town

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the pay word contains the soldier

parts.note: a wage is pay
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: Paying a soldier to stay on in a country town.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantage is a market town in Oxfordshire, birthplace of King Alfred.

clue.text: Cigar that's brown put back in Spanish dish

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, here the dish taking the colour inside

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: put backwards, so the word for brown is reversed

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A brown cigar returned to its place in a plate of Spanish food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses the colour word, and 'in' puts it inside the dish, the rice dish of Valencia.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin type of cigar.

clue.text: Expected score is capital!

parts.note: in golf, par is the expected score for a hole

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the anticipated score is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital!' looks like old-fashioned praise, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Fish hauled up caught with top of hook, as hanger-on

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled upwards means the fish word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an eel is a fish
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: An angler pulls in a fish caught on a hook that hangs on.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a parasite, so figuratively a sponger or hanger-on.

clue.text: Bread for elderly relative?

definitions.meaning: naan, also spelt ..., is a flatbread from South Asia
a grandmother, often informally called ... in Britain

explanation.surface: Bread being bought for an aged member of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is both a spelling of the Indian flatbread and a British pet name for a grandmother.

clue.text: Some assassin in Japan!

indicators.note: some of the words, so the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: A sly nod to a particular kind of Japanese killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a covert agent in feudal Japan, often hired as an assassin.

clue.text: Substitute showing restraint

definitions.meaning: a player kept on the bench to come on as a replacement

explanation.surface: A substitute player displays self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve is a stand-in player, and reserve is also reticence or self-restraint.

clue.text: Drug Jack fed to a horse the wrong way

indicators.note: facing backwards, so the whole assembly is reversed
something fed to another goes inside it, so the card letter goes into the other pieces

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A drug called Jack is given to a horse in the wrong manner.
explanation.walkthrough: J goes into A NAG to make AJNAG; 'the wrong way' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganja is a slang name for cannabis, a drug.

clue.text: Kind to tidy up

definitions.meaning: a kind is a type or variety

explanation.surface: An instruction to be kind when tidying.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a type or kind, and to sort things is to arrange or tidy them.

clue.text: Label in bank showing deficit

indicators.note: the label goes inside the bank word

parts.note: a shore is the bank of a sea or lake
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A label in a bank statement reveals an overdraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial, but it is the bank of a river or sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack or shortfall, the same idea as a deficit.
